answer: Timber-lot allocation: each identity must own a distinct registered log-lot with a felled-tree serial checked against a regional harvest ledger, and every action is signed by a cipher bound to that lot's recorded location and felling date. One operator cannot occupy two non-adjacent lots at once, nor fell timber in two counties on the same day without physical travel records contradicting the claim. Duplicate identities are caught when a known lotus of harvest data shows the same crew, equipment, or transport route serving both lots.
